references.text: The prophecy that the people will hear but not understand, and see but not perceive, parallels the condition of the Pharisees in John 9, where they hear Jesus' words yet remain spiritually blind.
The description of God's servant who will open the eyes of the blind contrasts with the Pharisees' claim to see, while they are actually blind to the truth.
Jesus' warning that if a blind person leads another blind person, both will fall into a pit illustrates the danger posed by the Pharisees as spiritual leaders who are themselves blind.
Jesus' condemnation of the Pharisees as 'blind guides' and 'blind' ones who do not see gold or pearls mirrors their own confession in John 9 about being blind.
